subject: Initial and last-used states of data
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 14.6.2.3.2 OK, case 2): static data is placed in initial state 'The first time the program in which it is described is activated after the execution of an activating statement referencing a program that possesses the initial attribute and directly or indirectly contains the program.' Code: ProgramTable.CallProgram, for n.Initial, creates a fresh instance and runs CancelContained(n) (every contained program recursively through CancelNode: instance dropped, static WS reset via StaticReset=__ResetStatics, internal connectors closed); the §14.9.18 GR2 implicit CANCEL at the INITIAL program's return does the same. The reset is applied eagerly at the container's activation rather than lazily at the containee's next activation - observationally identical because a containee is reachable only inside its container's activation. Probe probe/is3/p3.cob (INITIAL P3OUT > P3MID (non-recursive, WS M VALUE 0, internal file F) > P3IN (WS I VALUE 0)): second CALL P3OUT prints 'MID M=01 OPEN FS=00' / 'IN I=01' again - the INDIRECTLY contained P3IN is reset and P3MID's connector is in no open mode (reopen 00). Golden pb154_cancel_cascade pins the DIRECT half (RECURSIVE containee A returns to 0001 on the second CALL OUTER154); the INDIRECT half is probe-verified only (a spec-derived golden for the two-level case would harden the row). || REFUTED: CONFORMS with EMPTY test-ref (behaviour verified on legal source by probe; the cited golden is not a valid witness) — The behaviour holds on legal source: re-ran probe/is3/p3.cob with the pinned cobol.exe (INITIAL P3OUT > P3MID (file F, M VALUE 0) > P3IN): the second CALL P3OUT prints MID M=01 OPEN FS=00 / IN I=01 again. I also tried to break the eager CancelContained with a live containee (R RECURSIVE > I INITIAL > Q, Q CALLs R, R re-CALLs I while Q is active, which would throw EC-PROGRAM-CANCEL-ACTIVE). That source is illegal under 11.10.3 SR5, so the attack does not apply. The test-ref does not hold up: pb154_cancel_cascade pins the 'direct half' with INNERA154 RECURSIVE contained in OUTER154 INITIAL. 11.10.3 SR6 forbids that, so the golden's expected A=0001 comes from non-conforming source and is not spec-derived. The pinned compiler accepts that source without a diagnostic. BinderDriver.cs:412-415 checks only a unit's own INITIAL+RECURSIVE pair (COBOL0886), and its comment at ~427 wrongly calls an INITIAL containee of a recursive container legal. That is an under-reject defect with no kb/Work note found (grep of the pin's kb/Work for 11.10.3 SR5/SR6 found only PB899, about 0886). || editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (INITIAL attribute and contained programs exist at every edition; no Annex E change)
